name: Old Puffer
era: 1860s tank engine, more patch than plate. Somebody's grandfather drove it.

name: Tramway Engine
era: Skirted 1870s tram locomotive, built for cobbles, tolerates rails.

name: Yard Switcher
era: Early diesel-mechanical shunter. Loud, slow, tireless.

name: Iron Duke
era: Broad-gauge single-driver of the 1850s. Fast on the flat, proud on the hill.

name: Goods Mogul
era: 2-6-0 freight hauler. Nothing fancy, always on time.

name: Express Atlantic
era: 4-4-2 passenger racer pressed into freight work. Complains, delivers.

name: Consolidation
era: 2-8-0 mainline workhorse. Eight drivers, one purpose.

name: Ironclad Mallet
era: Articulated compound of the 1900s. Drags hills flat.

name: Boxcab Electric
era: Prototype electric, running on faith and a very long cable.

name: Streamliner
era: Shrouded 1930s express. A rumour with a whistle.

name: Coalbrook Titan
era: Twelve coupled drivers. The bridge inspector cries when it passes.
